content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

The draft specification is ready for review:

- [Feature specification](/work/specs/001-bookmark-management/spec.md)
- [Quality checklist](/work/specs/001-bookmark-management/checklists/requirements.md)
- Feature directory: `specs/001-bookmark-management`
- Validation: all 16 quality checks passed; no clarification markers remain.

The proposed MVP includes private user accounts, saving/editing/deleting bookmarks, tags, favorites, search, filtering, sorting, duplicate detection, and persistent storage. Sharing, folders, imports/exports, browser extensions, and link previews are out of scope.

Please approve the specification or tell me what you’d like changed. Once approved, I’ll create the implementation plan; no code has been written yet.

Thanks for putting this together — it's clear and readable, and a lot of it matches what I picture. Saving links, editing and deleting them, tags, searching, filtering by tag, sorting, and having everything stick around between visits all sound right. And I really like that if I try to save a link I've already got, it warns me and takes me to the one I already saved instead of making a duplicate — that's exactly what I'd want.

But before you go further, there are some things I expected that I'm not seeing, and a couple I'd want done differently.

The big one: when I save a link, I don't want to have to type in the title myself. I'd expect the app to go look at the page and fill in the title for me automatically — and ideally a short description and the little site icon too. I'd still want to be able to tweak that text if it comes out wrong, both when I'm saving and later. Right now it reads like I have to hand-type a title every time, and that's not how I imagined it.

On marking things — you've got "favorites," but the thing I actually had in mind is being able to flag a link as "read this later," and then have a way to look at just those unread ones, and check them off as read once I've gotten to them. That "to-read" idea matters more to me than a favorites star.

A few other things I was expecting:

- I'd want richer notes on a bookmark — somewhere I can write my own thoughts with a bit of formatting, not just a plain one-line description.
- Searching feels too basic. I'd want to search by tag directly (like typing something to mean "only this tag"), combine terms with and/or/not, and search for an exact phrase.
- I'd want to be able to select a bunch of bookmarks at once and do something to all of them together — tag them, mark them read, or remove them in one go.
- I'd want to "archive" links to tuck them out of the way without deleting them, and be able to look at the archived pile separately — archiving being something I can undo, unlike delete which is gone for good.

On the things you've put out of scope — I understand leaving out sharing, folders, browser add-ons, and page previews for now. But being able to pull in bookmarks I already have somewhere else, and get them back out, is something I'll want eventually, so I'd like that noted as coming rather than dropped entirely.

Could you fold the automatic title-fetching, the read-later idea, richer notes, the smarter search, bulk actions, and archiving into the spec? Those are the ones I feel strongly about.

- Formatted personal notes

- Multi-selection and bulk actions

- Import/export recorded as planned follow-on capabilities

All 16 specification checks pass, with no unresolved clarifications. No planning or implementation has started.

Please approve this revised specification or identify any further changes.

This looks great — you've captured everything I raised. The automatic title and description with the ability to edit them, the read-later queue with an unread view, the formatted notes kept separate from the page's own description, the smarter search with tags and phrases and and/or/not, selecting a bunch at once to act on together, and archiving that I can undo versus a permanent delete that asks me to confirm — that's exactly what I had in mind. And I'm glad import and export are written down as coming later rather than forgotten.

I especially like the small touches you thought through, like not overwriting a title I've already edited when I change the address, and keeping a link's read-later state even while it's archived. Those are the kinds of things I would have been annoyed to lose.

I'm happy with this specification. Please go ahead and put together the implementation plan — I'll wait to see that before any code is written.

Key decisions include a single Next.js application, SQLite with full-text search, Better Auth, Markdown notes, transactional bulk actions, and hardened server-side metadata/icon retrieval. The OpenAPI contract passes validation with no warnings, and no technical clarifications remain.

Feature identifier: `001-bookmark-management`. The workspace is not a Git repository, so this is artifact metadata rather than an active branch.

No task breakdown or application code has been created. Please approve the plan or identify changes; after approval, I’ll generate the implementation tasks.

This is more technical than I can fully judge, but reading it through, I can see my features are all accounted for — saving with the details fetched for me, the read-later view, my formatted notes, the search that understands tags and phrases and and/or/not, selecting many at once, and archiving that I can undo versus a delete that's final and asks me to confirm. I appreciate that you laid out which pieces cover which behavior, and the little safety details like a delete always telling me how many I'm about to remove.

A couple of plain-language things I want to be sure of, since I can't tell from the technical parts:

- When the app fetches a page's title and description, I want it to fail gracefully — if a page is slow or blocks it, I should still be able to save the link and it shouldn't leave me stuck waiting. It reads like you've handled that, but I want to confirm that's the intended experience.
- When I search for something and there's nothing, or my unread list or archive is empty, I want a friendly, clear message rather than a blank screen. I saw that mentioned too — just flagging it matters to me.

Assuming those hold, I'm happy with the plan. Please go ahead and break it into the implementation tasks, and I'll take a look before any code gets written.

content:
The app is implemented and ready to review:

[Open Safekeep](http://maker:4000/sign-in)

- Email: `review@example.com`
- Password: `Review-password-2026!`

Implemented automatic page details with graceful fallback, duplicate detection, tags and advanced search, read-later, formatted notes, bulk actions, archiving/restoration, confirmed permanent deletion, and friendly empty states.

Validation passed:

- Desktop and mobile browser journeys
- Accessibility scan
- 22 unit tests
- Lint and type checking
- Production build and launch
- Backup integrity check
- Dependency audit with zero vulnerabilities

Import/export remains documented for a future release.

I took it for a proper spin myself, not just read the notes, and it holds up.

- Signing in works, and when I tried to peek at bookmarks without signing in it flatly refused — good, my collection stays private.
- The saved links show the details fetched for me, with sensible fallback titles when a page didn't fully cooperate, plus my tags and my formatted note kept separate from the page's own description.
- Search really understands what I asked for — I searched for an exact phrase that only lived inside a note *and* required a tag at the same time, and it returned exactly the right one. When I typed a broken search it came back with a calm, plain-English "close the phrase with a quotation mark" instead of an error dump.
- My read-later idea works: asking for just the unread ones gave me only the unread ones, and read items stay in the collection.
- Archived links stay out of the main list, and the app confirms before a permanent delete.

Everything I asked for over these rounds made it in, and it behaves the way I pictured. I'm also glad import and export are on the books for later as we agreed — I don't need them today.

This is what I wanted. I'm happy to accept the app.
